teachings.title: The falling away first, and the corrupt versions
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: 2 Thessalonians 2 says the falling away and the man of sin come before the day of Christ, and modern versions that turn the falling away into rebellion and lawlessness set believers up to be seen as the rebels against the antichrist.
teachings.text:
Just touching on this theme:  The push for false Christianity that places salvation under the law, not under grace, the Noahide false religion, Hebrew Roots, Lordship/Repenting of sin, Judaizing, etc...is meant to bring about the falling away of believers, and pave the way for the antichrist and his false claim of being Jesus, returned.

In **2 Thessalonians 2**, we see the order and type of things to come:

*Now we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him,*

*2 That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand.*

*3 Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition;*

*4 Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.*

*5 Remember ye not, that, when I was yet with you, I told you these things?*

*6 And now ye know what withholdeth that he might be revealed in his time.*

Scripture says don't be deceived, no matter who you hear it from, the day of the Lord **will not** come until there is a falling away of believers, the antichrist revealed, *the man of sin* who will take the place of Jesus, naming himself God.

But the eschatology of false Christianity says what? That first Jesus comes, and the rapture either a "secret rapture" of the dispensationalist crowd, or a "symbolic event," not literal. Note, this all occurs in their false timeline before the rise of the antichrist, Great Tribulation, etc.

Now look at the same chapter and verse in the non-inspired version:

2 Thessalonians 2
New International Version

The Man of Lawlessness

Concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our being gathered to him, we ask you, brothers and sisters, 2 not to become easily unsettled or alarmed by the teaching allegedly from us—whether by a prophecy or by word of mouth or by letter—asserting that the day of the Lord has already come. 3 Don’t let anyone deceive you in any way, for that day will not come until the rebellion occurs and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the man doomed to destruction. 4 He will oppose and will exalt himself over everything that is called God or is worshiped, so that he sets himself up in God’s temple, proclaiming himself to be God. 5 Don’t you remember that when I was with you I used to tell you these things? 6 And now you know what is holding him back, so that he may be revealed at the proper time. 7 For the secret power of lawlessness is already at work; but the one who now holds it back will continue to do so till he is taken out of the way. 8 And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will overthrow with the breath of his mouth and destroy by the splendor of his coming.

Notice the heading, and throughout it talks about lawlessness, not sin. The falling away becomes "rebellion."

So if you were expecting the Second Coming first, before the Tribulation, and paint the picture of those who oppose the antichrist as lawless and rebellious, you can see how the stage is set for these false versions to fool all but the very elect. That believers who oppose the antichrist, who they will hail as Christ, and our rebelling against him, being against the law as a means of salvation, etc, we would be seen as the "bad guys" by these false believers under the beast's delusion, and the fraudulent Bible versions used to reinforce it to persecute those of us under grace.

This change from sin and falling away to "rebellion and lawlessness" is in the ESV, NASB, RSV.

*Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said..?*

teachings.title: He that endureth: saved out of tribulation
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: Jesus' promise that those who endure will be saved is, in context, physical deliverance of the saints from the tribulation at His coming, not a condition of spiritual salvation.
teachings.text:
Continuing, Jesus says, then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, to be killed, hated for His name's sake.

Although He is speaking to the disciples of their fate, remember that the context of this preaching is of the end times. Most Biblical prophecy has at least a double meaning, dual fulfillment. What many do is take the single application they want from it, out of the larger context to make the verses fit their preferred meaning.

And so, like with the beginning of sorrows we see the persecution of the saints spoken of by Jesus reflected in Revelation 6:9 and the souls of them that were slain for the word of God.

Jesus gives detail to the earthly experience of the martyrs and saints' persecution, where John gives us the Heavenly POV.

Christians will be hated by the world, even by family. False prophets will lead pogroms against us. Sin will run rampant, and many believers will fall away to avoid persecution, still saved but their love waxed cold. But we are encouraged to persevere through this tribulation, for in the end Jesus coming on the day of the Lord will save us from it.

This is, in context, physical salvation from the tribulation, not spiritual salvation. The false doctrine that claims only those who persevere are saved in a spiritual sense contradicts the context given.

teachings.title: Immediately after the tribulation of those days
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: Matthew 24 puts the great tribulation first and Christ's visible coming and the gathering of the saints immediately after it, with the darkened sun and moon of Revelation 6, refuting the pre-trib rapture.
teachings.text:
So continuing on with His prophecy, Jesus talks about "they" and "them" in Judea, fleeing what is called the "days of vengeance" in the parallel passage in Luke 21. It appears throughout the matching Gospel accounts that this is not referring to Christian believers but the Jews, as it's consistently othering pronouns. However, when talking about travel on the sabbath, He switches to "ye," the personal form, indicating the disciples and believers. I lean towards that the days of vengeance reflect both what happens to the unbelieving Jews in 70AD as well as their destruction in the end times of revelation, both. Regardless, it was also a time of tribulation for believers in Judea, and would be again when the beast turns his armies to betray the Jews, and take up his spot in Jerusalem, proclaiming himself God.

Jesus tells us this is the days of great tribulation, where He has not returned as yet, and the resurrection and rapture has yet to take place. Dispensationalists insist the Great Tribulation occurs after a secret second coming and rapture, despite these clear verses giving the order of things.

*For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be. And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect's sake those days shall be shortened.*

Again we see that this will be worse than anything that has ever occurred, and we have witnessed world wars with the deaths of tens of millions. The starvation and execution of tens of millions under Stalin and Mao. Greater than that. It's gonna be bad, and believers alive during this time will be mercifully saved by the shortening the time, 3 and a half years rather than 7. It is at this midpoint that the abomination of desolation occurs, whatever that may finally look like. We the believers will recognize it, but it has yet to come.

Jesus warns that during this time many false Christs and reports of His return will be made, but not be be fooled. That His coming will be like lightening that fills the entire sky. That it will be with a shout that is heard throughout the world. Every eye will see and ear hear His presence in the sky. He won't be in a hidden place, a cave, the wilderness. That His presence in the heavens will be like a carcass surrounded by carrion birds, as eagles, because He will be surrounded by the hosts of the saints caught up with Him in the clouds. (Rapture is just a Latin term meaning 'caught up,' for those special boys who say 'acctuuuually, rapture doesn't appear in the Bible!")

Now with these caveats, Jesus begins to reveal what will happen on the Day of the Lord.

*Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken.*

Note the timing is AFTER THE TRIBULATION. Not before. Pre-trib rapture heresy BTFO with one verse, straight from Christ's mouth.

We see the parallel in **Revelation 6**:

*And I beheld when he had opened the sixth seal, and, lo, there was a great earthquake; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon became as blood; And the stars of heaven fell unto the earth, even as a fig tree casteth her untimely figs, when she is shaken of a mighty wind. And the heaven departed as a scroll when it is rolled together; and every mountain and island were moved out of their places.*

The sun and moon darkened is a common theme throughout the end times Bible prophecy, it is the common feature of all mentions of the Day of the Lord, second coming. It is an unmistakable sign that cannot be faked, and has not taken place in history of creation. Those claiming that the prophecy is past, that the resurrection has already taken place, that Jesus has already returned and we are in the millennium now, or had been, are all dependant on ignoring this incredible occurrence.

teachings.title: Revealed from heaven in flaming fire
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: 2 Thessalonians 1 lines up with Matthew 24 and Revelation 6: out of tribulation Christ is revealed from heaven, gathers the living and resurrected saints, and takes vengeance on the disobedient.
teachings.text:
In 2nd Thessalonians, Paul, Silvanus and Timothy writing unto the church in Thessalonica to encourage them in their faith, through all the persecution and tribulations they endure.

These early believers, who accepted and obeyed the Gospel of faith towards Jesus, as given by the Apostle and evangelists, were beset by persecution, tribulation by man, suffering for God. To bolster their spirit, Paul writes to remind them that patience, enduring troubles is a blessing, a manifestation of the righteous judgement of God, that they may be counted worthy of the kingdom of Heaven, to which we as believers belong.

That we have the promise from God that all those unrighteous who trouble us as believers will be recompensed for what they've done, on that great and terrible day, when Jesus returns.

Tying in to the timing of that day to the preaching of Jesus in Matthew 24, we see the concurrency of events, and just as Revelation 6, a slightly different perspective of the same events.

Out of tribulation, the Lord Jesus will be revealed from Heaven with His mighty angels, taking vengeance with flaming fire on them that know not God and are disobedient to the Gospel of Jesus Christ our Lord.

Again, we see Jesus returning as he ascended, in the clouds but with a noise and sight to behold by all the world, and the gathering of the resurrected believers and those saints alive, saved from tribulation by His return:

**Matthew 24:30-31**
*And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.*

**Revelation 1:7** *Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him. Even so, Amen.*

**1 Thessalonians 4:16-17**
*For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.*

teachings.title: Let no man deceive you: these come first
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: Scripture says the falling away and the revealing of the man of sin come before the day of the Lord, so believers are to watch the signs as the fig tree instead of trusting the pre-trib imminence teaching.
teachings.text:
And so we see the timing of things leading us to this day, the clock already ticking towards this inevitable event.

But the patience of the saints is tried, today just as it was in the first century. And as Jesus warned the disciples regarding the timing of the end of the world, "*Take heed that no man deceive you,*" so to does Paul echo Christ's sentiment;

*Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition; Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.*

No man knowth the day or hour that these things will come to pass, but the false teachings of the imminency of Christ's return given by the pre-trib dispensationalists ignores the signs of the times the Bible tells us to watch for. That once certain events come to pass, we may know the day of the Lord is at hand.

Let no man deceive you. These things happen first. This is consistently taught in scripture regarding end times Bible prophecy. That we are as the watchmen, sober and vigilant that we may recognize the times as they come.

**Matthew 24:32-33**
*Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh: So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.*

We know there will be a falling away, a great apostasy. We know that iniquity shall abound, worse and worse. We know that the man of sin will be revealed. That he should conquer the world, set himself up as God and his mark be issued, that all who do not believe on Christ will worship him as God.

*And then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming:*

*Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders, And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved. And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.*

And the Bible says that there will come at the midpoint of the Great Tribulation, Daniel's prophecy of the abomination of desolation, in the midst of Jerusalem. Jesus says those who have eyes to see will understand, and that this signals the coming of the Lord.

But to those who are not saved, to the perishing, Jesus will come upon them as a thief in the night.

*But as the days of Noah were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.*

*For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.*

And so, Jesus encourages us to be vigilant that we may know the signs and prepare;

*Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come. But know this, that if the goodman of the house had known in what watch the thief would come, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken up. Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh.*

*Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord hath made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season?*

*Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.*

*Verily I say unto you, That he shall make him ruler over all his goods.*

*But and if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; And shall begin to smite his fellowservants, and to eat and drink with the drunken; The lord of that servant shall come in a day when he looketh not for him, and in an hour that he is not aware of,*

teachings.title: The false hope of escaping tribulation
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: All who live godly will suffer, and the Left Behind hope of a secret rapture before the worst is a snare belonging to lukewarm churches and drunken watchmen.
teachings.text:
There's obviously more to say on this, the subject of end times prophecy is exhaustive and deep. But the fundamentals, the tribulations we will suffer, now and in the Great Tribulation, must be. All who live Godly will be persecuted for His name's sake. Jesus came to divide, even from family, who will hate us, and give us up to judgement of the wicked.

The false hope that we will not be made to suffer for the faith, that we will be secretly raptured ala Left Behind, and not be present for the worst of it, is part and parcel with the lukewarm churches, the drunken watchmen, those who win no souls, gather no wheat for the harvest, who sit in laser light fun-centers, being told faithless affirmations by vipers who deny the power of Christ's blood...that false hope to avoid troubles is a snare and a stumbling block. And to them the end truly will come as a thief in the night.

teachings.title: The abomination of desolation is the sign
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: The sign to watch for is the abomination of desolation, then the darkening of sun and moon and Christ's visible return to gather the elect after the great tribulation.
teachings.text:
Now, having laid out these stipulations, Jesus has given so that we may not be deceived into thinking His return was imminent, He segues to the actual day of the Lord they asked of.

*When ye shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not, (let him that readeth understand)*

The parenthetical statement of for our benefit. We who are still here on Earth when it comes will understand. This is the sign we look for. Not false messiahs. Not wars or famines or earthquakes. Not persecution that seems overwhelming. Not betrayals by family and friends, or hatred of us for His name.

These things will always occur. They must be.

But when we see the abomination of desolation stand where it ought not, we should know the day of the Lord is nigh.

Jesus warns that all who may be in Judea should flee, shifting His focus from 'ye' to 'they.' That those present there shouldn't even take time to grab their coat. This is described in the parallel passage of **Luke 21** as "the days of Vengeance" and it is my belief, comparing scripture with Mark, Luke and Matthew 24, that the vengeance is upon the Jews for their role in setting up the beast to put the abomination of desolation in the midst of Jerusalem. The antichrist turning on them and destroying them. Either way, it's yet another sign when it comes upon them.

And *Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.*

There is a lot of speculation as to what this means, but it seems pretty cut and dry. Jerusalem was trodden down by Rome, an empire of Gentiles, and it remains so, under Jews who say they are but are not. They that are in Judea. Until the harvest. Until the fullness of the Gentiles has come. When the increase is gathered, the sheaves brought in. The day of the Lord is the harvest.

With all biblical end times prophecy there is dual fulfillment, and as we see frequently throughout the Bible, things that fit prophecy are but a picture of the thing to come. But even understanding this, I still see this as fairly straightforward prophecy, given the frequent analogies of the harvest. The fullness of the season.

*And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring; Men's hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.*

And Jesus says this is when you know for sure that His coming is soon. There are those who say that the resurrection is passed, or that we are already in the millennial reign. The Sun and Moon darkening is the consistent signal the day of the Lord is here throughout the Old Testament prophecy and the New. This has not happened. And what follows certainly has never happened. The triumphant return of Jesus in the clouds, visible to all men.

*And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.*
*And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.*

This is the sign. This is how you know for sure. This is the Great Tribulation such as never has been, followed by Sun and Moon darkening, and Christ's return and the gathering of the elect. The fullness of the Gentiles come in.

teachings.title: In those days, after that tribulation
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: Mark 13 plainly places the darkening of the heavens, Christ's coming and the gathering of His elect after the tribulation.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Mark 13**;

*And except that the Lord had shortened those days, no flesh should be saved: but for the elect's sake, whom he hath chosen, he hath shortened the days.*

*And then if any man shall say to you, Lo, here is Christ; or, lo, he is there; believe him not:  For false Christs and false prophets shall rise, and shall shew signs and wonders, to seduce, if it were possible, even the elect. But take ye heed: behold, I have foretold you all things.*

Jesus says again, don't be fooled. *Behold, I have foretold you all things.*

And so, knowing these things he has foretold us, and keeping His warnings in mind, we can know when His day is near, for He gives us the signs and the timing.

..*In those days, after that tribulation, the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, And the stars of heaven shall fall, and the powers that are in heaven shall be shaken. And then shall they see the Son of man coming in the clouds with great power and glory. And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.*

In those days. AFTER the tribulation. The return. The rapture. The promise of eternal life given in the day of redemption, the Great Day of the Lord come at last! Amen.

teachings.title: Heresies Drawn from Revelation 4
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: Revelation 4:1 is John alone in the spirit, not a pre-trib rapture, and the chapter gives no support to Catholic vain repetitions, soul sleep or gnosticism.
teachings.text:
Some additional **Revelation 4** notes, particularly on heresy.

Pre-trib rapture dispensationalists will use the taking up of John to Heaven to claim this is the secret rapture, that not only John but all the saved, are gathered at verse 1. They have to point to this event, because the following chapter, **Revelation 5**, begins the opening of the seals and the tribulation that follows. But **Revelation 4:1**-**2** says nothing about the gathering of the elect (we will see that it is immediately after the tribulation, when the sun and moon are darkened).

*After this I looked, and, behold, a door was opened in heaven: and the first voice which I heard was as it were of a trumpet talking with me; which said, Come up hither, and I will shew thee things which must be hereafter. And immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne.*

This is not the bodily resurrection of the saved, glorified unto God and gathered on the day of redemption. It is John, alone and in the spirit. Pre-trib rapture is a foolish doctrine.

Another heresy justified out of **Revelation 4**, the vain and repetitive prayers offered by Catholics. Jesus tells us in **Matthew 6:7**; *But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.*

Many Catholics will point to the praise given "without ceasing" by the 4 seraphim, the creatures before the throne of the Lord as a nullifying text that contradicts Jesus' instruction to us on prayer, and so repetitive speed-muttering "Hail Mary's" and the occasional "Our Father" until they become a mush of words used as an incantation to their idols they worship kneeling before them, is ok. It's preposterous. We shall praise the Lord without ceasing but that's not vain repetitions, but giving honor and glory to Christ.  In prayer here, in this life, we should follow the model of conversational praise, gratitude and petition laid out by Jesus, in the manner described.

Another heresy is the idea that when we die bodily, that our soul sleeps or something, rather than being in the presence of the Lord as the Bible says in **2 Corinthians 5** that to be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord, and we see that there are men, in Heaven, the 24 Elders for example. (They are not the only souls in Heaven as we will see moving forward in **Revelation**)

We can also dismiss the wicked heresy of gnosticism, that "matter is all evil," because we see, again, scripture has a different idea of creation, that God looked upon what He made and it was good. Here in **Revelation 4** we see it in the praise given by the elders; *for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created.*

The Lord God does not take pleasure in the wicked.

teachings.title: The Seals Line Up with Matthew 24
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: The seals track the Olivet discourse, and the sixth seal's darkened sun and moon mark the gathering of the elect immediately after the tribulation.
teachings.text:
And then, back in **Revelation**, we see the 5th seal opened, and John is shown an altar in Heaven, and under the altar, standing before the Lord, are the souls of the martyrs who were slain for the Word of God. For their testimony that Jesus is Christ, that God's promise is true.

Again, in **Matthew 24***:*

*9 Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake.*

*10 And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.*

The events revealed in the seals tracking what Jesus gave as signs that the Apostles be not deceived.

*15 When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)*

*16 Then let them which be in Judaea flee into the mountains*

Jerusalem is conquered, Jesus shifts from the "thees" and "ye's" of believers to "they" and "them" of the Jews in Jerusalem fleeing to the mountains. The abomination of desolation set up before them. (These are the days of vengeance, and we will talk about that more in the second half of **Revelation)**

But continuing the narrative from **Revelation 6**, the 6th seal is opened and we are shown there is a great earthquake and the sun and moon are darkened. The stars falling from the heavens. **Matthew 24**:

*29 Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:*

*30 And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.*

*31 And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.*

Immediately AFTER THE TRIBULATION the sun and moon are darkened and the elect are gathered unto Jesus, returning in the clouds. The rapture. The timing of it is plain and we see it reflected here (and in **Revelation 7**) but back to the narrative of chapter 6:

*And the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men, and every bondman, and every free man, hid themselves in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains; And said to the mountains and rocks, Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?*

So we see that in **Matthew 24**, (also **Luke 21** and **Mark 13** for parallel passages) that the timeline for tribulation and the Great Tribulation line up with Revelation. It's interesting that the only Gospel that does not have the Olivette discourse, Jesus preaching end times prophecy, is the Gospel of John. Instead he is given an entire book of revelations from Christ.

teachings.title: The Secret Pre-Trib Rapture Is Heresy
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: The day of the Lord is visible to all and begins the wrath, so a secret rapture sparing the saints the tribulation is a wicked heresy.
teachings.text:
The day of the Lord, Christ's return to gather the elect and the beginning of the wrath to come, poured out on the earth has begun. I don't have time now to go over the significance of the day of the Lord. How it is mentioned throughout scripture and always is accompanied by the sun and moon darkening, and a great shout heard by all. A return visible to the whole world. And the wrath that follows.

But suffice to say that the secret pre-trib rapture, that Jesus sneaks in and quietly disappears the saved so that they don't experience the wars, famine, pestilence, earthquakes and Great Tribulation of being persecuted for His sake, is a wicked heresy out of the pits of Hell.  In the next chapter we will see from John's vantage in Heaven that the raptured saints appear by the multitudes before the throne. After the first six seals are opened. After the tribulation of those days.

The 7th seal has yet to be opened....

teachings.title: The Multitude Appears After the Sixth Seal
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: The raptured multitude appears in heaven after the six seals and before the seventh seal's wrath, in sequence, proving a post-trib, pre-wrath rapture.
teachings.text:
After the sealing of the 144,000, we see the raptured souls of the saint appear in Heaven before the throne of the Lord.

*After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands; And cried with a loud voice, saying, Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb.*

This is the day of redemption. The gathering of the elect on the great and terrible day of the Lord.

Again note the order. They arrive after the tribulation, after the 6 seals, on the day of the Lord. Before the wrath, which only comes after the 7th seal is opened. It is a post-trib, pre-wrath rapture.

Some false doctrine states that this chapter is out of sequence with 6 and 8. That it happens at a different time, or that it's some kind of separate vision. They have to to make their false doctrine of pre-trib or post-wrath rapture fit the narrative's timeline.

But chapter 7 opens with "*And after these things.."* which places it firmly in sequential order to chapter 6. Verse 9 continues the timeline with "*After this*
.." all one narrative.

teachings.title: They Came Out of Great Tribulation
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: The elder says the multitude came out of great tribulation, which puts to bed pre-trib, post-wrath, preterist and millennial errors.
teachings.text:
But finally, who are the mixed multitudes, of every kindred and tongue, who suddenly appear before the throne in white linen, praising and worshiping the Savior? Of this there is no question, for John is told:

*And one of the elders answered, saying unto me, What are these which are arrayed in white robes? and whence came they?*

*And I said unto him, Sir, thou knowest. And he said to me, These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.Therefore are they before the throne of God, and serve him day and night in his temple: and he that sitteth on the throne shall dwell among them.*

They are the saints, the believers who came out of the great tribulation, saved by the return of Jesus, gathering His elect. There is no doubt that can be had that this should put the pre-trib (and post-wrath, preterist, amillennial, post millennial, "rapture isn't in the Bible!" "It's symbolic!") nonsense heresies to bed.

And we are given the greatest of encouragements, the blessed hope we can count on as saved, born again believers;

*They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more; neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat. For the Lamb which is in the midst of the throne shall feed them, and shall lead them unto living fountains of waters: and God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes.*

Amen!

teachings.title: Daniel 12 and Revelation 10 Are Bookends
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: Daniel 12 and Revelation 10 show the same vision from both ends of the seven years, from the tribulation and deliverance to the finishing of the mystery.
teachings.text:
So here in **Revelation 10** we see what seems to be the bookend to **Daniel 12**, which was the scripture being expounded upon by Jesus in the Olivette discourse.

In Daniel 12, we get a recap of what's happening from the fall to the Great Tribulation, and the salvation of the resurrection; the rapture of the saints.

Daniel references the fall of Satan, cast out by Michael, which we will study further when the book of Revelation rewinds a bit and changes focus in chapter 12.

So we see the order of things in Daniel, and that casting out of the devil and his 3rd of the angels is what precipitates the Great Tribulation. The Bible tells us that Satan, currently, is before the throne of God day and night, accusing the righteous, and here on the earth *as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.*

This changes when he is cast down, and knowing his time is short, seeks to damn as many as possible while persecuting the sons of God on this world before he is chained in the pit of Hell and tormented for a millennium.

And so, as we will see he promotes the false prophet, the antichrist to power to war against the saints. And *there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time.* Or as Jesus puts it, *then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be.*

And then,  *at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book. And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt. And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.*

Daniel, like John, sees an angel standing on a waters edge. One foot in the water, the other one land. Daniel sees another on the opposite shore and a man clothed in white linen on the waters between.

The one closest to Daniel asks the *man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters,* *How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?*

The man in linens on the water swears to heaven that this trouble, this tribulation, shall last *for a time, times, and an half,* or 3.5 years. And when Satan has done his worst to scatter the power of the holy people, all those things shown Daniel, the tribulation and rapture, will be finished. 1,260 days from the triumph of the antichrist, setting up the abomination of desolation and the persecution of the saints, until the gathering of the elect and the coming of Christ in the clouds.
Then 3.658 years, or 1335 days will follow. This appears to be the division of Daniel's 70 Weeks, or 7 years, that makes up the time of Great Tribulation and the wrath; the judgments and woes.

Daniel says he doesn't understand what he sees, or what he's being told, and he is instructed to seal this up and to basically not worry about it, until the time is finished.

But John appears to see the second angel across the waters from the one on Daniel's shore. And while the one Daniel heard tells him *the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end,* the angel John hears says that *there should be time no longer: But in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he shall begin to sound, the mystery of God should be finished, as he hath declared to his servants the prophets.*

Bookends. I wonder if John was on one bank of the waters, and Daniel on the other at the same time, relatively speaking. Having a shared vision, one of the beginning of the 7 years, the other the end, seeing it finished with the 7th trumpet to come, the final woe.

teachings.title: Pre-Trib Gives a False Security
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: Early Christians faced death unafraid, but the pre-trib rapture and other end-times errors give a false comfort that leaves people unready.
teachings.text:
A quick aside: early Christians were accused by the Jews to the Romans of being a death cult. They cited the lack of fear of those who believed when threatened with death if they didn't renounce their faith in Christ.

As we know from reading the book of Acts, they stoned believers to death, beheaded them, and persecuted the same as always. They gathered mobs of reprobates to attack them in the streets and in their homes. They chased them from city to city. They persecuted them refusing to allow them to preach the gospel that others may be saved.

And the faith they showed in this persecution to never once repent but rather suffer bondage injury and death, terrified those who persecuted them. Leading to the accusations of being a death cult. Not knowing that it was rather faith in eternal life.

How many Christians today, living in the comfort that we know could suffer this type of persecution and maintain their testimony?

One of the reasons that the pre-tribulation rapture is pushed so hard by the beast is to add to that comfort a false sense of security that they won't know tribulation. That they'll be taken up to heaven before having to suffer for their faith.

In fact, most of the false doctrines surrounding end times Bible prophecy including preterism or amillennialism and post millennialism, create that false sense of security in those professing to be Christian.

And to those that buy into it, and don't stay in the word and in prayer, to them they will be taken by events like a thief in the night. Like the bridesmaids who didn't have oil for their lamp. And many risk being shut out of the feast of the bridegroom.

teachings.title: Pre-Trib Dispensationalism Undone by Scripture
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: The rapture is immediately after the tribulation, not before, and dispensationalism rests on the heresy that Jews are saved by bloodline rather than by grace through faith.
teachings.text:
Pre-triber Dispensationalists would have us interpret these scriptures, the rise of the antichrist, the abomination of desolation, the mark and the war on the saints of the Great Tribulation ...that Jesus tells us about in the Gospels and again in Revelation... as happening AFTER the saints are raptured. That the seals representing the antichrist, war, famine, death leading up to Christ's return in the clouds, and the wrath that follows the day of the Lord, all take place only for the Jews. The "righteous remnant," AND the apostate Israel alike. That when scripture says "*so all Israel shall be saved*" it means the modern state of Jews who say they are but are not, that is a synagogue of Satan.

They claim that Matthew 24 and its parallel passages in Luke and Mark are written to the Jew. That they are the saints who will refuse the mark. Gentile believers having been secretly spirited away before any of this begins.

But as we have read through Revelation we can see the clear chronology given. None of the pre-trib Schofield judaized version of end times makes any sense. It doesn't fit the timelines given throughout scripture. And a secret rapture is never mentioned. It is "*Immediately after the tribulation*," according to Jesus'own words. We see the saints killed for His testimony described as the faithful. Not some unbelieving Jews.

The only fate that awaits apostate Israel is the days of vengeance that Christ promises *us* believers will befall *them*, the Jews. That, as the Bible says, the wrath of God is upon them to the uttermost.

The pre-tribulation heresy and the rest of dispensationalism that rests upon it is undone by God's word. And the foundation of it is the wicked doctrine that different people are given salvation and eternal life by God in different ways.

That God's grace extends to Gentiles by faith, but to the Jews by being the seed of Abraham. By their genetics. This is damnable heresy. Salvation has always come by grace through faith, calling upon the name of the Lord. And the salvation of Abraham's seed is fulfilled in Christ Jesus.

teachings.title: Recap of the End Times Timeline
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: He sets out the full order of events: sorrows, the beast, the Great Tribulation, rapture after the tribulation, then the 144,000 and three and a half years of wrath.
teachings.text:
So let's recap.

There is tribulation on the earth. Satan is cast down, shut out of Heaven with a 3rd of the Heavenly host. The beginning of sorrows is here. Wars and rumors of war, pestilence and famine. Millions dead. This lasts nearly three and a half years.

A man who goes forth conquering and to conquer comes to prominence. He brings an offer of peace and safety. The governments of this world give him power. He is fatally wounded and then is restored to life by Satan, likely possessed. A counterfeit Christ.

He secures a one world government. His false prophet establishes a one world religion that worships the antichrist, the beast, as God. The abomination of desolation is set up and the whole world wonders after the beast. This is the end of the first 42 months. Those who are watching the signs know their salvation is at hand.

The two witnesses appear and begin to preach the word of God, halting rain and calling down fire. Destroying those who seek to harm them with fire from their mouths.

The beast and his prophet set up a one world currency with the mark, all for the express purpose of waging war on the remnant of the woman's seed, the believers who have the testimony of Jesus Christ. They who will refuse to worship the beast and take the mark. This is the Great Tribulation.

Multitudes of Christians are killed for their faith, the patience of the saints is tried. 75 days into the Great Tribulation, the sun and moon are darkened and Jesus Christ returns in the clouds with a shout. His angels gather the elect from the four corners of the world. The time of harvest has come. First the dead in Christ, then those who are alive and remain, all are caught up, "raptured," into the clouds to meet Jesus. Their bodies transformed in a twinkling of an eye to glorified bodies. Redeemed. The mixed multitudes of those resurrected appear in Heaven singing glory to the Lord. The day of His wrath has come.

The 144,000 in Heaven are sealed with the name of their Father. They are protected from the wrath that will be poured out while they are on earth. The trumpet judgments (and the vial judgments) follow. And for the rest of the second three and a half years, God's wrath is poured out.

The beast, still in power, tries to keep the people under his thumb. Eventually, near the very end, he will kill the two witnesses and they will lay dead for 3.5 days as the world watches, celebrating their deaths believing they are the cause of the woes. Then God raises them up glorified, and they are taken up into heaven. Then Jesus and His saints come to claim His kingdom.

There are more details coming in the remaining 8 chapters, but I just wanted to get us all up to speed. I may have left something out, and please forgive me if I have. This recap is as much for my benefit as anyone reading it.

As we see in today's chapter, 14, there is the destruction of Babylon yet to come, the beast and Satan cast into the pit, the millennial reign and the final battle, the White Throne Judgment and final triumph to come. Hang in there.

teachings.title: As the lightning: no secret coming of Christ
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: Christ's return will be seen by all like lightning, with the saints gathered as Noah and Lot were taken before destruction, so the pre-trib secret rapture is a deception.
teachings.text:
When should the Kingdom of God come?

Jesus, asked this question of the Pharisees, says that the kingdom isn't an earthly kingdom. It is within us to be part of it. It is spirit. It is in our hearts. We who are saved are of the Kingdom. Jesus taught His disciples that when we do good in the service of the Lord unto others, the Kingdom is nigh unto them. When a people reject the Gospel, Jesus said to shake off the dust, telling them that the Kingdom was nigh unto them.

We carry the Kingdom of God in our hearts and the key to its entrance in the truth of the gospel.  It sounds corny and sappy to modern ears, just as much as it did the scoffers and mockers of Christ's day. They expected an earthly kingdom led by an earthly king. They saw their religion as being about political power and breaking free of Roman oppression and the restoration of Judea. Their faith in wealth and man.

But Jesus Christ came to offer something greater.

But knowing the impatience of man, and the weight of the world on even the most devout, Jesus offers us the hope of His glorious return, the coming of His wrath, and the gathering of the elect in the resurrection and rapture.

Jesus teaching on n end times prophecy is most extensively given in **Matthew 24**, but Luke's telling has the fundamentals and added insight.

Jesus says as weary and impatient as we may be, don't be fooled. If someone comes claiming a secret return of Christ, not to believe them because Jesus will appear as the lightening that spans to all edges of the sky. Unmistakable. All will see His return.

The dispensationalist heresy of a pre-trib rapture relies on a secret coming of Christ, which sets men up for being fooled by the antichrist. Let no man deceive you.

Jesus return will be for the unbelieving like the days of Noah, where everyone went about their business, until Noah and his family were taken in to the ark as sudden destruction came up on the rest. The wrath of God poured out from Heaven.

The same with Sodom, where the wicked vexed just Lot with their filthy behavior, and the people there did what people do, right up to the day Lot and his family were spirited away, gathered by angels, and fire rained down destroying the wicked cities.

2 Peter 3:3-6
*Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts, And saying, Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation. For this they willingly are ignorant of, that by the word of God the heavens were of old, and the earth standing out of the water and in the water: Whereby the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished*

Jesus says, in that day of the Lord at His return, which will be manifest to all, we who are saved will be gathered, like birds of carrion to a corpse. Where Christ is in the clouds we will go to Him, caught up together. And woe to those who turn back. Who doubt. Who like Lot's wife turn to their old life and things. Who believed in vain and put the things of this world before the kingdom. Those seeking to save their life lose it.

Make sure you know where you stand.

teachings.title: Lift up your heads: signs before His coming
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: Jesus' Luke 21 prophecy gives signs, persecution of believers and Jerusalem's desolation before He comes in the clouds to gather the saved, while woe comes on the Jews.
teachings.text:
Here in **Luke 21** we get another telling of Jesus preaching end times prophecy, something we have covered extensively in teaching on [Matthew 24](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/7894) and our Revelation series.

This more condensed version covers all the main points Jesus made to His disciples, both in short term and long term prophecy.

But first, Jesus points out the poor woman giving offering of tithes to the temple treasury, that her giving all she had, despite it being little, gave more than the rich man throwing in great wealth which was a fraction of his treasures.

Then, as some disciples are in wonder if the richness of the Temple in Jerusalem, Jesus says that it will be destroyed, with not one stone left upon another. This was fulfilled literally in 70AD, but with ramifications that echo into the future end times. 70 AD was a foreshadowing of the days of vengeance to come against the Jews.

Jesus builds from the common place wars and rumors of war, earthquakes in diverse places, plagues and pestilence. False Christs arising that fool all but the elect. Signs from heaven. Jesus says be not afraid.

And they will take Jesus disciples, then and in the future, and persecute them for His name's sake. He says not to prepare what to say, He will give them a month of wisdom. The Holy Ghost speaking through them.

He mentions again the idea that in our tribulation we who believe will be betrayed, even by family. He has come to divide, and parents will hate children and children parents and all manner of kin and friend and neighbor who takes the mark and worships the beast will betray those who believe.

*And ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake.*

But we shall not perish. We have eternal life.

A sign we will know the end is near, Jerusalem will be made desolate by the Gentiles. The days of vengeance, when the beast and his armies betray the Jews who helped put the antichrist into power, wrath upon those people.

The signs in the sun and the moon and the stars, which we see elsewhere describes the sun and moon darkening, stars blotted out, that these are a sign His return is imminent. Like a fig tree reveals the signs of the times of the season, so will these events of great tribulation and the wonders in heaven that follow. That men will die of fear.

*And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.* Amen!

Jesus tells us what to watch for, and to rejoice knowing our day of redemption, which the Holy Spirit has sealed us unto, that the promised resurrection draws nigh.

This is an encouragement for we who are saved. To the Jew, "those people," Jesus says they will be destroyed and woe unto them, but to us the glory of Jesus returning to gather us with Him in the clouds is something we should watch for in hopeful expectation, that we be ready. Worthy to escape the wrath that shall come to pass and stand before Jesus that wonderful day.

teachings.title: Not imminent: the signs before His return
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: The thief in the night is for the unprepared; Christ gave signs to watch, the seals and great tribulation, before His coming gathers the elect and the wrath begins, so imminence and pre-trib are deceptions.
teachings.text:
*And they asked him, saying, Master, but when shall these things be? and what sign will there be when these things shall come to pass?*

One quick point I would like to make is in regards to the false doctrine of Jesus imminent return. That he could come at any moment, right now.

Dispensationalists teach a pre-tribulation rapture wherein Christ comes to the believers as a thief in the night. That is not supported by scripture. The thief and the night is in reference to those caught unawares. Those who are not prepared for his coming. They won't recognize the signs of the times and won't be prepared to meet him.

But for believers we are given what to watch for. If you know what Jesus's disciples are asking here in verse 7, They say teach us what to look for. In Jesus compares his teaching to the fig tree. That you can tell the season and when to expect the fruit. He lays out all of these things that must come to pass before the end. Before his return and the day of redemption. He gives us this information that we be not deceived. And if you think about it, The idea that we cannot know when he's coming and that there won't be signs that we can observe, that he will come secretly, and rescue believers from tribulations of man, is a great deception.

Jesus here lays out the timing of things, the first four seals, The four horsemen. The Antichrist, wars on a global scale, famine and pestilence, megadeth. The affliction of the entire world by Satan and his forces.

Then, at the fifth seal we see a shift where Satan's attention is no longer on all of mankind, but specifically believers. This is the great tribulation. This is where we will suffer for his name's sake. And it is His coming in the clouds that saves us. He comes with great signs and wonders in heaven, the sun and moon darkening, coming with a shout and in full glory seen by every man. The day of the Lord. The Rapture. The gathering of the elect into the clouds with him and the seventh seal marking the beginning of the wrath of God.

Scripture lays out a 3 and 1/2-year period where we who are alive and remain can know His return is soon. These things that must come to pass.

So stay sober and vigilant and watch for the signs of the times, in your patience, be ready for the return of the Lord.

teachings.title: Psalm 7 and the day of the Lord
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: Psalm 7 prophesies the day of the Lord, when after the tribulation Christ returns and the resurrected and living saints are caught up to compass Him about in the air before the wrath.
teachings.text:
**Psalms 7:6–9**
*Arise, O LORD, in thine anger, lift up thyself because of the rage of mine enemies: and awake for me to the judgment that thou hast commanded. So shall the congregation of the people compass thee about: for their sakes therefore return thou on high. The LORD shall judge the people: judge me, O LORD, according to my righteousness, and according to mine integrity that is in me. Oh let the wickedness of the wicked come to an end; but establish the just: for the righteous God trieth the hearts and reins.*

This passage in **Psalms 7** is prophetic to the day of the Lord, Jesus' second coming, the rapture and the wrath.

The congregation of the people, the resurrection of the saints, gathered together in the air to meet Him at His glorious coming.

**Matthew 24:27–31**
*For as the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be. For wheresoever the carcase is, there will the eagles be gathered together. Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.*

As eagles, carrion birds, circle a carcass, so will the risen saints "compass about" Jesus, as we meet Him in the air. When He returns with His own, the spirits of the dead, raising them first, and then those which are alive and remain:

**1 Thessalonians 4:14–17**
*For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him. For this we say unto you by the word of the Lord, that we which are alive and remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not prevent them which are asleep. For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.*

David looked forward to this day of judgement, the day of the Lord. The day of redemption.

teachings.title: Christ the King of all the earth
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: Psalm 47 prophesies Jesus, who is God, ascending with a shout and returning with a trumpet to catch up the saints, reign as King of kings over every nation, and finally deliver the kingdom to the Father.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 47** is a song of praise for the Lord, the King of kings. Christ Jesus, Who shall put every nation under His feet.

**Revelation 11:15–17**
*And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever. And the four and twenty elders, which sat before God on their seats, fell upon their faces, and worshipped God, Saying, We give thee thanks, O LORD God Almighty, which art, and wast, and art to come; because thou hast taken to thee thy great power, and hast reigned.*

He shall rule and reign with a rod of iron, and give to all His people their inheritance in His Kingdom.

Jesus is God. Verse 5 says *God is gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet.* A prophetic Old Testament verse, made clear in the New Testament, carrying the comfort of all believers;

**1 Thessalonians 4:16–17**
*For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.*

We shall sing of the glories of the Lord, forever.

**Revelation 7:10–12**
*And cried with a loud voice, saying, Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb. And all the angels stood round about the throne, and about the elders and the four beasts, and fell before the throne on their faces, and worshipped God, Saying, Amen: Blessing, and glory, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, and honour, and power, and might, be unto our God for ever and ever. Amen.*

**Revelation 19:16**
*And he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.*

For Jesus is the King of all the earth, and reigns over the heathen. All the nations. He is greatly exalted above every name.

**Philippians 2:9–11**
*Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.*

Jesus will reign over all things, and, having defeated death and been made ruler of all, He will give all to God the Father. A perfect sacrifice, holy and acceptable, made holy by His righteousness:

**1 Corinthians 15:24–27**
*Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power. For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet. The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death. For he hath put all things under his feet. But when he saith all things are put under him, it is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him*.

**Psalm 47** is a wonderful and prophetic song of praise and worship for the Kingdom of God, under our Lord Christ Jesus. All honor and praise is His. Amen

teachings.title: Gather my saints together unto me
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: Psalm 50, a prophecy of Asaph the seer in God's own voice, shows Christ the Creator returning in fire to judge, and the gathering of His saints before His wrath is poured out, proving the rapture is no new doctrine.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 50**, is a song written directly from the voice of God to His people, His own perspective directly to man. It is instruction in doctrine and prophecy, by His word. In the first person.

He spoke these things through a psalmist other than David. The superscript titles this as "A Psalm of Asaph," making it the very first of the 12 "Asaphite Psalms" in the Bible.

Asaph was a prominent Levite, appointed by King David as the chief musician and worship leader before the Ark of the Covenant when it was brought to Jerusalem. More than just a song director, the Bible credits him as a prophet. A seer.

**2 Chronicles 29:30**
*Moreover Hezekiah the king and the princes commanded the Levites to sing praise unto the LORD with the words of David, and of Asaph the seer. And they sang praises with gladness, and they bowed their heads and worshipped.*

While prophesying may refer to preaching the word of God, seer is the specific term for a visionary who is given glimpses of the future by God, prophetic understanding of things that are not but will be.

He begins his song by introducing its Author. The mighty God. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, it is God breathed, and spoken. But this will be the word of God, as a message of judgment for His people.

It establishes first the primacy of God, the Creator. By His Word the earth and the heavens were made.

**John 1:1–4**
*In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made. In him was life; and the life was the light of men.*

It is important when we see credit for creation to God in the Bible, to remember that this includes Jesus.

**1 Corinthians 8:6**
*But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.*

We have a New Testament understanding when we reflect on the Old Testament revelations. The nature of the Godhead is revealed in the creation. And it is relevant to this Psalm.

Out of Zion, the place God chose to put His name, God hath shined.

His presence in the Tabernacle and the eventual Temple, God with His people through their worship, is an echo to the true coming of the Lord in the flesh, and His return on His day to judge the nations, upon that holy mountain.

*Our God shall come, and shall not keep silence: a fire shall devour before him, and it shall be very tempestuous round about him.*

The Second Coming, the return of Christ, is the day we all look forward to with gladness. He will come with power, a consuming fire proceeding from Him, and the sword of His word from His mouth shall slay the wicked.

**2 Thessalonians 1:7–9**
*And to you who are troubled rest with us, when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels, In flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ: Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power*

The future judgment of the world was a key part of the Israelites understanding, though through a glass darkly. However, having the full revelation of the complete Bible, we see clearly what they only glimpsed in faith.

He comes as a judge, the Son calling up to Heaven, and down to Earth, with a shout, with trumpet, the call to judgment of His people, before His wrath is poured out on the world.

*Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice. And the heavens shall declare his righteousness: for God is judge himself. Selah.*

The gathering of the elect, those sanctified by the Spirit in Christ, is not a "new doctrine," as some would claim. The Rapture, or the gathering of the elect being caught up together to meet the Lord in the air, was a key part of prophecy for the Lord's people.

teachings.title: The Trumpets Are Wrath, Not Tribulation
teachings.theme: The day of His wrath
teachings.summary: The trumpet judgments are God's wrath fuelled by the saints' prayers and cannot be confused with the tribulation, and Revelation is meant to reveal.
teachings.text:
God's wrath, the trumpets of war, sounding 7 times (similar to the battle of Jericho where they sounded trumpets 7 times around the city). Only 4 in, and so far there is massive destruction. Unnatural natural disasters. This is the wrath of God fueled by the prayers of the saints. It cannot be confused with the tribulation, even that great tribulation that came just prior to the day of the Lord.

When we get to the second half of the book of Revelation, we will see the 7 vial judgments which, when compared to the 7 trumpet judgments, we will see they are complimentary, in how they affect the earth and its remaining inhabitants, and in their timing. (Chapters 12-22 retell much of 1-11, from a different vantage point, with added details)

It is important to see how things progress, and how the timing is consistent with other scripture that talks about end times Bible prophecy, and just how clear the things stated are. We may see through a glass darkly, but we are given quite a lot of details and signs to watch for, and an order of things that is clear when taken in context. God is not the author of confusion. Revelation means to reveal, not to obscure.

teachings.title: The Plagues of Egypt Picture God's Wrath
teachings.theme: The day of His wrath
teachings.summary: The plagues of Egypt picture the wrath poured out in the trumpets, as prophecy often has dual fulfilment.
teachings.text:
Also, for those unfamiliar with Exodus 5-10 and the 10 plagues that afflicted Egypt due to the harness of Pharoah's heart, mirror or provide a picture of the judgements poured out on the earth during the days of God's wrath.

The 10 plagues of Egypt in order are: water turning to blood, frogs, lice, flies, livestock pestilence, boils, hail, locusts, darkness, and the killing of firstborn children.

We can already see the water turning to blood, hail and darkness in these first 4 trumps. The exodus of Hebrews from Egypt is a picture of salvation, and a picture of the end times. Most Bible prophecy has dual fulfilment or multiple fulfilments, as the scriptures exist to teach us what was, what is and what shall come.

It's all connected and beautifully so.

teachings.title: Still They Repented Not
teachings.theme: The day of His wrath
teachings.summary: Even in His wrath God seeks repentance, yet hardened men refuse, and believers should study the timing themselves rather than lean on others.
teachings.text:
The Bible tells us that *The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.*

Even in His wrath and judgment upon the Earth, He seeks repentance of those being afflicted for their wicked hearts. And as we see in Revelation 9, despite the supernatural destruction, the signs and wonders in Heaven, the resurrection of the dead and gathering in the clouds of the elect, the woes and all, the men of the earth will still refuse. Stiff-necked and hearts hardened.

Some folks you just can't reach.

We will see in the following chapter the two witnesses appear in all this, and call the people to repentance preaching in His name. I believe the 144,000 likely are sent to minister the Gospel to those few on Earth who do repent during this time, the three and a half years of wrath before the millennial reign begins.

Of the timing; we know the day of the Lord begins the trumpet judgments. The initial destruction and fire and hail happening quickly. But the 5th trump, the first woe, lasts on earth 5 months (the remaining months of the 4th year, the day of the Lord coming slightly more than 3 and a half years into the Great Tribulation)

Then the armies of God come against man for a year and a month and a day and an hour.

I admit the granular indexing of the exact days and weeks, reflected in Daniels 70 Weeks prophecy from **Daniel 9** can make my eyes glaze over. But people more autistic than I have charted it out and found the days and years matching up with Revelation, and the events foretold. While it is fascinating to consider and a testament to the awesome precision of God's word, I won't get out over my skis trying to explain it. But we can see from these verses there is a timing of things. A way to know when and how long each thing happens.

One of the ways false doctrines evolve surrounding these events is that many are like me, and daunted by some of the more seemingly esoteric aspects, and so they lean heavily on other's interpretation, rather than studying it out themselves.

So make the effort to read and compare scripture with scripture yourself, even if you only get the gist of the timing. Because God reveals it openly. Do not be deceived.

teachings.title: The Winepress of the Wrath of God
teachings.theme: The day of His wrath
teachings.summary: As Abel's blood cried from the ground, the innocent blood of the martyrs brings the grapes of wrath to ripeness.
teachings.text:
But there is another harvest; from the vineyard of the Lord, the grapes of wrath.

*17 And another angel came out of the temple which is in heaven, he also having a sharp sickle.*

*18 And another angel came out from the altar, which had power over fire; and cried with a loud cry to him that had the sharp sickle, saying, Thrust in thy sharp sickle, and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth; for her grapes are fully ripe.*

*19 And the angel thrust in his sickle into the earth, and gathered the vine of the earth, and cast it into the great winepress of the wrath of God.*

*20 And the winepress was trodden without the city, and blood came out of the winepress, even unto the horse bridles, by the space of a thousand and six hundred furlongs.*

Glory, glory, hallelujah.

We know from Cain and Abel in Genesis that the blood of innocents spilled in the earth cries out for God's vengeance. This is a theme repeated in scripture, and the innocent blood of the tribulation and especially that of the martyrs slain in the Great Tribulation, brings the grapes of the vine to fruition. The wrath of God come full. And the winepress is trodden, and the blood that pours out is sufficient to fill a 1,600 furlongs, up to a horse's bridles. A furlong represents a Grecian/Roman measure of a stadia, or 660 feet, thus this measure quoted is 1,000,000 feet. The height of a bridle being 6 feet. That's a lot of blood.

The winepress and the reaping are symbolic of the events like the rapture and the wrath that we see described in more understandable detail elsewhere, but it gives picture to what it actually means and the scope of it all that man's limited mind can comprehend God's awesome work.

teachings.title: The Song of Moses and the Song of the Lamb
teachings.theme: The day of His wrath
teachings.summary: The song of Moses is likely Deuteronomy 32, prophesying wrath on Israel for rejecting the Rock, and the song of the Lamb is the new song of Revelation 5.
teachings.text:
*And they sing the song of Moses the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb...*

What are these songs? Many interpret this as one song, but it's clearly stating there are two being sung, one of Moses and the other of the Lamb.

We know that Moses in the Old Testament is credited with two songs. One is sung by Moses and the Israelites upon their successful flight from Egypt giving praise to God for delivering them and warning the nations of the promised land of God's might. This is told in Exodus 15.

The other, in **Deuteronomy 32** which I quoted a couple posts ago, is sung to give everlasting doctrine, that it be sung for all ages by the Israelites to remind them of the Rock of their salvation and prophecy of God's wrath upon them when they eventually forsake God, His law and reject the Messiah, the Christ, who is the Rock. I really suggest going back and reading it again, and consider how clear and prophetic it is regarding precisely what will happen, the apostasy of Israel, the coming of Jesus, and God's destruction of the Jews who don't believe and His wrath on those who reject Jesus.

Most who preach on this subject say the song of Moses is the first song from Exodus, and maybe it is. It's a victory song praising God, but it makes far more sense that the song found in Deuteronomy 32 would be sung just as Jesus' victory is coming, the wrath of God about to be delivered. The judgment of nations which is literally part of the song.

Of course, most who preach on end times Bible prophecy are dispensationalist Zionists who believe the false and wicked doctrine that the end times are a victory for the Jews, rather than Jesus.

The song of the Lamb I believe is the new song mentioned in **Revelation 5**, which we were told was given to the angels and elders to sing, and was entirely about how worthy and great Christ Jesus is to be given this power and glory:

*Saying with a loud voice, Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.*

Given it is literally a song of the Lamb, it just makes sense this is what John is referring to.

teachings.title: The Vials Align with the Trumpets
teachings.theme: The day of His wrath
teachings.summary: The seven vials parallel the seven trumpets in the same wrath period, poured on the damned who harden their hearts rather than repent.
teachings.text:
The 7 vial judgments of the Lord. His wrath and recompense for sin. As all who remain on the earth either worshiped the beast and took the mark, damning themselves or remained unsaved up unto the end of Great Tribulation and the rapture, they and the earth itself suffer the righteous anger and just judgment of the Lord. It is fitting punishment that the saints in Heaven had prayed for, giving glory to the Lord for His wrath has come.

These 7 vials align with the 7 trumpet judgments of chapters 8-11.

Trumpet 1, Vial 1
Trumpet 2, Vial 2
Trumpet 3, Vial 3
Trumpet 4, Vial 4
Trumpet 5, Vial 5
Trumpet 6, Vial 6
Trumpet 7, Vial 7

And are poured out in the same three and a half year period, the second half of Daniel's 70 Weeks. And as we can compare, many of the vials match or enhance the trumpet judgments. There is overlap to the destruction John witnesses and describes.

The first trumpet brings fire to the earth and burns up a third of the trees and all green grass. The vial brings grievous sores upon those with the mark. A judgment of the earth and of man.

The 2nd trump, a mountain burning with fire is cast into the sea, turning a 3rd of the oceans to blood, killing sea life and destroying a third of ships. The 2nd vial, the seas all become blood and all life therein dies. The stink of putrid fish and rancid blood overwhelming the earth.

The third trump and vial; the rivers and fountains of waters, the fresh water of the world, are destroyed. Wormwood making a third of the waters bitter and poisonous, the vial turning the rest to blood that the unrighteous be given blood to drink for they have shed the blood of the saints and prophets and are worthy to have blood to drink.

The fourth trumpet and the fourth vial are poured out upon the sun, and it is given the angels the power to smite the sun and stars and moon that a 3rd of their light is dimmed, and the heat from the sun scorches the wicked who curse God rather than repent and give Him glory in His wrath.

Note that the vast majority this happens to are damned. Twice-dead. They aren't being punished to bring a saving repentance spirituality, admitting they were wrong and that Christ is Lord won't save their souls. But even as these plagues fall upon them, the Bible says, they will remain stiff-necked and hearts hardened. Defiant in their error. Cleaving to their sin. They deserve everything they get.

Darkness comes from both the fifth trumpet and the fifth vial. Abaddon opens the Pitt and the smoke rises up to blot out the dimmed light of the sun. And the beast, the antichrist who still remains on his throne during this period of wrath, sees his kingdom left in darkness. And they that worship the beast blaspheme the name of God for their pains and sores and repent not.

During the sixth trumpet and the sixth vial, you see the great river Euphrates mentioned for both. The river is dried up with the sixth vial and four angels that had been bound beneath the Euphrates are loosed with the sixth trumpet.

As the 7th trumpet sounds and the 7th vial are poured, we see lightnings, voices, thunderings, an earthquake, and great hail. Hail the size of a talent.

The heavy common talent, used in New Testament times, was 58.9 kg (129 lb 14 oz).

Wew.

teachings.title: The battle of Armageddon
teachings.theme: The day of His wrath
teachings.summary: At Armageddon Christ defeats the beast's armies with the sword of His mouth, casting the antichrist and false prophet into the lake of fire and leaving the wicked to the fowls.
teachings.text:
**Isaiah 13:9**
*Behold, the day of the LORD cometh, cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate: and he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it.*

**Joel 3:12-14**
